question: Should OpenClaw own this experimental grouped-Claw lifecycle planner, including the versioned plan-integrity and capability-consent contract, as a core surface before the dependent apply slice proceeds?
rationale: The branch adds a new core CLI and machine-readable lifecycle contract across config, state, packages, MCP, cron, and capability escalation; code review alone cannot establish the intended permanent product and owner boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the core experiment
options.body: Keep the planner in core, require final-head redacted human and JSON runtime proof, and review the stacked diagnostics/apply sequence as one lifecycle contract.

options.title: Narrow to generic seams
options.body: Retain only reusable read-only ownership or planning primitives in core and move optional grouped-package orchestration to an external plugin or package surface.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Defer the lifecycle surface until the open RFC and ownership model receive an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core experiment
recommendation.body: Keep the planner in core, require final-head redacted human and JSON runtime proof, and review the stacked diagnostics/apply sequence as one lifecycle contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned and supplied the substantive ownership and provenance review that this contract implements.
